identity.title: TokSuite: Measuring the Impact of Tokenizer Choice on Language Model Behavior

problem.claim: The paper examines how tokenizer choice influences language-model performance and behavior.

gap.claim: The influence of tokenization is poorly understood because it is difficult to measure in isolation.

contributions.claim: TokSuite releases fourteen pre-trained models differing in off-the-shelf tokenizer while matching architecture, dataset, training budget, and initialization.
TokSuite includes a multilingual robustness benchmark covering real-world perturbations in English, Chinese, Farsi, Italian, and Turkish, curated by native annotators.
The collection is intended to decouple tokenizer influence and support analysis of benefits and shortcomings across popular tokenizers.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that TokSuite supports novel findings about the respective benefits and shortcomings of a wide range of popular tokenizers.

narrative_sequence.summary: Tokenizers underlie text representation, yet their isolated effect on language-model performance and behavior remains poorly understood.
The authors present TokSuite as models and a benchmark for studying tokenization’s influence.
They release fourteen models that vary tokenizer choice while holding major training factors constant.
They release a native-annotator-curated multilingual benchmark for perturbation robustness across five languages.
They characterize the combined resources as enabling tokenizer decoupling and novel comparative findings.

source_observation.claim: The abstract addresses isolation difficulty with models that differ in tokenizer while sharing architecture, dataset, training budget, and initialization.

lessons.interpretation: Matched resource construction can make a causal factor easier to study by reducing confounding differences.
lessons.application: When introducing a benchmark for one design choice, release matched variants that hold salient training and model factors fixed.
lessons.exception: This approach is unsuitable when the design choice inherently requires changing those factors or when matched variants cannot represent deployment conditions.

unknowns: The abstract does not report the specific empirical findings, metrics, or tokenizer comparisons enabled by TokSuite.
It does not state how robustness scores are computed or how the fourteen tokenizers are distributed across languages.
